name: Education
summary: AI labs ship study modes and fund training at scale, governments add AI to schooling, universities return to proctored exams, and trials suggest AI tutors help only when constrained and supervised.

regions.name: AI tutors
regions.summary: OpenAI and Google ship tutoring modes that guide rather than answer, and Khan Academy is building Khanmigo features on Gemini. Trials favor AI that works alongside human tutors.

landmarks.name: ChatGPT study mode
landmarks.summary: OpenAI launched a study mode that uses Socratic questions and step-by-step prompts instead of direct answers, for Free, Plus, Pro and Team users, with Edu to follow.

landmarks.name: Gemini Guided Learning
landmarks.summary: Google added Guided Learning to the Gemini app, a tutoring mode built on its education-tuned LearnLM work that breaks problems into steps and checks understanding.

landmarks.name: Khan Academy builds Khanmigo tools on Gemini
landmarks.summary: After a partnership announced in January 2026, Google and Khan Academy shipped Gemini-based interactive diagrams and a rebuilt practice tool in Khanmigo for back to school.

landmarks.name: Tutor CoPilot RCT
landmarks.summary: Preregistered trial with 900 tutors and 1,800 K-12 students found AI suggestions to human tutors raised topic mastery 4 points, and up to 9 for weaker tutors. Working paper.

regions.whyItMatters: Tutoring modes are how most students now meet AI, and their design decides whether it supports learning or replaces the effort.
regions.openQuestion: Will students choose a mode that makes them work when a direct answer is one click away?

deepDives.title: AI tutoring in UK classrooms: exploratory RCT (Eedi, DeepMind)
deepDives.why: Shows how a supervised LearnLM tutor was run and measured against human tutors in real schools.

deepDives.title: Tutor CoPilot study page (Stanford NSSA)
deepDives.why: Readable account of the human-plus-AI tutoring model and its measured effects.

deepDives.title: Khan Academy blog on its Google.org partnership
deepDives.why: Khan Academy's own account of what the Gemini-based Khanmigo tools do for students and teachers.

regions.name: Assessment & cheating
regions.summary: Universities are stepping back from AI detectors, which courts and campuses have found unreliable as sole evidence, and returning to proctored, in-person exams.

landmarks.name: Princeton ends 133 years of unproctored exams
landmarks.summary: Princeton faculty voted almost unanimously to proctor all in-person exams from 1 July 2026, the first time since its Honor Code began in 1893, citing AI-enabled cheating.

landmarks.name: Stanford moves to proctored exams
landmarks.summary: Stanford said it would begin proctoring in-person exams after a pilot that grew from seven courses in 2024 to more than 50, its first shift from unproctored exams since 1921.

landmarks.name: Curtin University turns off AI detection
landmarks.summary: Curtin in Australia disabled Turnitin's AI writing detection across all campuses from 1 January 2026, keeping text-matching checks, as several universities did the same.

landmarks.name: Court voids sanction based on Turnitin flag
landmarks.summary: In Newby v. Adelphi University, a New York state judge threw out sanctions on a student whose paper Turnitin flagged as 100% AI, faulting the university's process.

regions.whyItMatters: How schools verify that work is a student's own shapes what degrees certify and how much AI use is treated as misconduct.
regions.openQuestion: Can take-home and written coursework be assessed credibly at all, or only work done under supervision?

deepDives.title: Vanderbilt: why we disabled Turnitin's AI detector
deepDives.why: An early, widely cited explanation of the false-positive and transparency problems with detectors.

deepDives.title: Matter of Newby v. Adelphi University (decision)
deepDives.why: The court's own reasoning on what process a university owes a student accused through an AI detector.

deepDives.title: Plagiarism Today on the Adelphi case
deepDives.why: Long-running academic integrity blog that tracks AI misconduct disputes and what they mean.

regions.name: School & university policy
regions.summary: Governments are requiring AI education in schools and giving students and teachers access to AI tools, often in partnership with AI companies.

landmarks.name: US executive order on AI education
landmarks.summary: EO 14277 created a White House task force on AI education, called for a Presidential AI Challenge and told agencies to prioritize AI in teacher training grants.

landmarks.name: Beijing requires AI classes in schools
landmarks.summary: Beijing's education commission required at least eight class hours of AI instruction a year in primary and secondary schools from the fall 2025 semester.

landmarks.name: Estonia AI Leap
landmarks.summary: National program giving about 20,000 students in grades 10-11 and their teachers free AI tools from September 2025, with OpenAI as a partner and expansion planned for 2026.

regions.whyItMatters: National mandates and vendor partnerships set which AI tools a generation of students grows up using, and on whose terms.
regions.openQuestion: Do national rollouts improve learning, or mainly lock school systems into particular vendors?

deepDives.title: EO 14277 text in the Federal Register
deepDives.why: The exact duties and deadlines the US order sets for the task force and federal agencies.

deepDives.title: Eurydice: Estonia's AI Leap initiative
deepDives.why: EU education network's summary of how Estonia structured its national AI rollout.

deepDives.title: ERR: how will AI Leap change schools?
deepDives.why: Estonian public broadcaster's explainer on the aims, partners and concerns around the program.

regions.name: Upskilling & workforce learning
regions.summary: AI companies are funding large training programs and credentials for workers and teachers, with stated goals in the tens of millions of people. Outcomes are not yet measured.

landmarks.name: Microsoft Elevate $4B commitment
landmarks.summary: Microsoft pledged more than $4B in cash and technology over five years for AI education and skilling, with a goal of helping 20 million people earn AI credentials.

landmarks.name: OpenAI certifications and jobs platform
landmarks.summary: OpenAI announced AI certifications through OpenAI Academy and plans for a jobs platform by mid-2026, committing to certify 10 million Americans by 2030 with Walmart as a partner.

landmarks.name: AFT National Academy for AI Instruction
landmarks.summary: Teachers union AFT announced a $23M academy funded by Microsoft ($12.5M), OpenAI ($10M) and Anthropic ($0.5M), aiming to reach 400,000 educators in five years.

regions.whyItMatters: Vendor-funded training is becoming the main route by which workers and teachers learn AI, which shapes what counts as AI skill.
regions.openQuestion: Do vendor-issued AI credentials lead to better jobs or teaching, and who checks that independently?

deepDives.title: OpenAI: expanding economic opportunity with AI
deepDives.why: The company's own statement of its certification targets, partners and jobs platform plan.

deepDives.title: AFT press release on the AI academy
deepDives.why: The union's account of the academy's funding, governance and training goals.

regions.name: Evidence on learning outcomes
regions.summary: Controlled trials are accumulating. Unrestricted chatbots can hurt later unaided performance, while constrained or supervised tutors show gains in small, short studies.

landmarks.name: Unguarded AI can harm learning (PNAS)
landmarks.summary: Peer-reviewed field experiment with nearly 1,000 high school math students: standard GPT-4 access cut later unaided grades by 17%, while a guardrailed tutor largely avoided this.

landmarks.name: Harvard physics AI tutor RCT
landmarks.summary: Crossover RCT in Scientific Reports (N=194): students using a custom GPT-4 tutor learned more than twice as much, in less time, as in an active learning class. Two topics only.

landmarks.name: Eedi and Google DeepMind tutoring RCT
landmarks.summary: Exploratory trial with 165 students in five UK schools: a tutor-supervised LearnLM solved 66.2% of later novel problems versus 60.7% with human tutors alone. Preprint.

landmarks.name: World Bank GPT-4 tutoring RCT in Nigeria
landmarks.summary: Randomized trial of a six-week, teacher-supervised after-school program using GPT-4 in nine Edo State schools reported sizable gains in English. Working paper.

regions.whyItMatters: Billions are being spent on AI in classrooms on the strength of a handful of short trials, so what the evidence shows matters.
regions.openQuestion: Do gains from constrained AI tutors persist over a school year and replicate outside small, supervised trials?

deepDives.title: OECD Digital Education Outlook 2026
deepDives.why: Synthesis of the trial evidence, separating general chatbots from purpose-built education tools.

deepDives.why: The study team's plain account of the program, its results and what made it work.

deepDives.why: Cross-country review of what generative AI does and does not do for learning, teaching and administration.

deepDives.title: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning
deepDives.why: Open version of the PNAS field experiment that anchors the debate on chatbots as a crutch.

deepDives.why: Plain summary of a large RCT on AI that assists human tutors rather than replacing them.
